title: backlog.py tidy starts one git status per removable worktree, so its git processes grow with the number of leftovers
goal: backlog.py tidy without --apply reads the state of 60 recorded leftover worktrees that every other check leaves removable with at most 40 git processes, a fixed number however many leftovers there are

run:
import os,shutil,subprocess as s,sys,tempfile,pathlib as P
N=60
t=P.Path(tempfile.mkdtemp());c=t/"clone";c.mkdir()
shutil.copytree("_tools",c/"_tools",ignore=shutil.ignore_patterns("__pycache__","test_*"))
shutil.copy("backlog.json",c/"backlog.json")
(c/"kb/_self/backlog").mkdir(parents=True);(c/"kb/_self/backlog/.keep").write_text("")
def g(*a):return s.run(["git",*a],cwd=c,check=True,capture_output=True)
g("init","-q","-b","main");g("config","user.email","a@b.c");g("config","user.name","t");g("add","-A");g("commit","-q","-m","base")
for i in range(N):
    iid="ST-p%07d"%i
    (c/"kb/_self/backlog"/(iid+".json")).write_text('{"id": "%s", "kind": "story", "title": "x", "status": "done"}' % iid)
    g("worktree","add","-q","-b","work/"+iid,".claude/worktrees/agent-"+iid,"HEAD")
    s.run([sys.executable,"_tools/backlog.py","own",str(c/".claude/worktrees"/("agent-"+iid)),"--class","worktree","--item",iid],cwd=c,capture_output=True,check=True)
d=t/"bin";d.mkdir();log=d/"n";w=d/"git"
w.write_text("#!/bin/sh\necho x >> %s\nexec %s \"$@\"\n"%(log,shutil.which("git")));w.chmod(0o755)
env=dict(os.environ,PATH=str(d)+os.pathsep+os.environ["PATH"])
bad=[]
for name,argv in (("backlog.py tidy",["_tools/backlog.py","tidy","--older-than","0"]),("kbmon.py cleanup panel",["_tools/kbmon.py","--once","--panel","cleanup"])):
    log.write_text("")
    p=s.run([sys.executable]+argv,cwd=c,env=env,capture_output=True,text=True)
    n=len(log.read_text().split())
    print(name,"started",n,"git processes for",N,"recorded worktrees and branches (exit",p.returncode,")")
    if p.returncode or n>40:bad.append(name)
sys.exit(1 if bad else 0)

notes: Found by the SP-vmtfnkim review on 2026-10-26 (BG-xgpnkgth, whose gate g1 answer keeps one git status for each worktree every other check leaves removable): the item's check plants 30 leftovers that are not removable (their items are open), so it counts 13 processes; with 60 leftovers whose items are done and which are clean, merged and idle, tidy --older-than 0 starts 73 git processes, one status each. The repro plants that. No verdict changes and no data is at risk; the process count grows with the removable leftovers, which the goal's fixed number says it should not. A fix needs a way to read the dirtiness of many worktrees in a fixed number of processes, or a bounded goal.
